recipes.name: Disney’s Ratatouille
ingredients_raw: salt and ground black pepper to taste
1 small eggplant, trimmed and very thinly sliced
1 zucchini, trimmed and very thinly sliced
1 yellow squash, trimmed and very thinly sliced
1 red bell pepper, cored and very thinly sliced
1 yellow bell pepper, cored and very thinly sliced
1 teaspoon fresh thyme leaves, or to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Spread tomato paste onto the bottom of a 10-inch baking dish. Sprinkle with onion and garlic. Stir in water and 1 tablespoon olive oil until thoroughly combined. Season with salt and pepper.

Arrange alternating slices of eggplant, zucchini, yellow squash, red bell pepper, and yellow bell pepper, starting at the outer edge of the dish and working concentrically towards the center. Overlap slices a little to display colors.
Drizzle vegetables with remaining 3 tablespoons olive oil; season with salt and pepper. Sprinkle with thyme leaves. Cover vegetables with a piece of parchment paper cut to fit inside.
Bake in the preheated oven until vegetables are roasted and tender, about 45 minutes. Serve with dollops of mascarpone cheese.

raw_recipe.headline: Disney’s Ratatouille
raw_recipe.description: Ratatouille is a rich and elegant French summer vegetable and tomato side dish made by baking sliced eggplant, zucchini, and squash until tender.

review.reviewBody: We loved this dish! I'm ten and I made this for my family. It was so easy to do that I would do it again every night!!!!! We did not tomato paste so we used a jar of pizza quick sauce which worked great!

I omitted the tomato paste and added a can of crushed tomatoes. I made a sauce with the red/yellow bell pepper, onion, garlic, oregano, basil, salt and pepper by sautéing and then used my immersion blender to smooth it out a bit. I served this with a saucy fettuccine alfredo. It was a hit

This was a 5/5 we have made this dish many times adding other veggies such as slices of purple onion and cremini mushrooms- rather than drizzle olive oil over top I lightly brush one side of the cut veggies with garlic and olive oil mix, I do not put any cheese on at all while baking but sprinkle Parmesan over top when serving. It’s an easy and delicious dish

This is a very good "BASIC" recipe for a beginning cook for sure and the style is the only way to go !!! delightful and so glad to see an aspiring young cook to try it too!!! ... my teen and I make it together however because I am an old timer I know a few tricks and these are some good additions if you want to spice it up... as typically Ratatouille has its herbal base with fresh basil and thyme and garlic in olive oil herbal mix over top while baking... SO with that being said.. instead of tomato paste base in the bottom try a bit of change up and use "crushed tomatoes" which I make myself if I don't have on hand by pulsing diced or stewed tomatoes with 3 oz of tomato paste ... adding that to sauteed diced onion/garlic/yellow and red peppers/ ...adding fresh or dried basil; thyme; parsley... salt and pepper... simmer while you are thinly slicing the egg plant; zucchini; yellow squash and tomato ... I also pour about a 1/2 cup Olive oil before I do anything and add 2 minced garlic cloves and fresh or dried basil; thyme and parsley and let it sit while I work... this is the topping after arranging everything... I add the red sauce to the sauteed diced veges and pour into the 9 X 13 then arrange the thinly sliced veges alternating in any order either in rounds or ovals ..drizzle my olive oil herbal mix over all cover and bake at 375 for 40 mins uncover bake another 20 and then grate fresh parmesan and or other white cheese and let set 10 mins and serve!!! DELIGHTFUL

My kids typically refuse to eat summer squashes. They LOVED this dish! Luckily I have a mandolin which made the veggies very evenly sliced. I substituted a really good marinara for the tomato paste, and added fresh sage and oregano to the thyme sprinkled on top. I also added some Parmesan during the last 15 minutes. Can't wait to make it again.

Made just like recipe says although with some minor changes. I only had green bell peppers and did not have the round baking dish so I used a square baking dish. Also did not have any marscapone so used shredded mozzarella and freshly grated Parmesan. Was really good! My daughter went back for seconds and she is not a huge fan of squash or eggplant. I lightly salted the eggplant and squash before baking and let them sit for about 20 min to draw out of some the moisture. I also sautéed the onions and garlic as others suggested. So delicious with fresh veggies from the local farmers market! Served it with green beans also from a local farmer and a whole roasted chicken I did in the slow cooker also from this website as I was using the oven for this dish.

OMG... this smelled so good as it was baking and tasted just as good! Family loved it. I did it a bit differently, sauce as written but with 1 cup of water and added fresh basil.I layered the veggies (eggplant,mushrooms, peppers,zucchini,tomato & more fresh basil- in that order. Baked with the parchment paper as written. Will be making again. Note- this is GREAT as written, I only change it to use what was on hand from my garden!
I love this recipe, but make a few changes. I add sliced tofu and mushrooms instead of eggplant, sprinkle with parmesan and mozarella, serve it over quinoa for extra protein

This was delicious! After reading several reviews, I cheated a bit and used Classico Four Cheese Pasta sauce instead of the tomato paste , water and oil but closely followed the recipe otherwise. No yellow squash available but used all veggies mentioned in the recipe plus I added red onion slices, Roma tomato and thinly sliced potatoes as well. Sprayed the layer with Pam, spiced top with salt, pepper, garlic and onion powder and thyme leaves. Added crumbled Feta to the top. It was a big hit! I think I would omit the potato next time - they stayed a little too firm in comparison to the texture of the other vegetables. I would try mushrooms, too, next time - and there will be a next time - soon!

I did a few things different based on what I had on hand, not necessarily preference. I didn’t have tomato paste so I used a can of tomato sauce. I seasoned the tomato sauce with freeze dried Italian herb seasoning blend, freeze dried basil, salt, black pepper, fennel seeds and Trader Joe’s umami seasoning. I used a red onion and sliced it instead of chopping. I used two yellow squash, one zucchini and red & orange bell peppers. I salted the eggplant for 30 minutes then rinsed and dried it. I peeled the eggplant and squash. I baked it in an 8x12 baking dish and covered it with foil for 40 minutes then took the foil off for 10 minutes. I topped with goat cheese. Mmmm mmmm, so good!

First time I have used this recipe for the sauce, and this sauce was so easy and delicious. As far as the veggies, in addition to looking beautiful, they tasted wonderful. I used a regular eggplant the first time I made it, and a Japanese eggplant the second time. Absolutely do not omit the eggplant, it adds so much flavor. I also used Roma tomatoes in addition to the peppers. I found a great sheep's milk feta cheese which I used instead of the mascarpone.
New favorite
Made this. Took a bit of time. I dried the vegetables and used homemade marinara instead of the paste. It was beautiful but a bit mushy. I would maybe cook it uncovered next time!

I made this the night before for a mother's day pitch in and it was very tasty. I added a small purple onion to the layers and some freshly shredded parmesan at the end. It was even better the next day.

Loved it… delicious and gorgeous!!! Used what.veggies I had on hand, along with a good spicy marinara instead of the tomato paste base. Don’t tell any purists, but I added a pound of browned ground beef to the marinara, because I was feeding a teenage boy and didn’t want to make a separate protein dish. We watched the movie while scarfing it down.
I have made this recipe a couple of times and everyone raves about it.
thin sliced chayote would also be nutricious
I made my pet rat help me and it taste delicious
I can't say enough about how this turned out. I followed the video (very helpful). The taste was amazing. I served it with crusty bread and a nice light French Wine. It was a hit.
This recipe is easy and beautiful.. If you want to make it easier, use a mandoline to slice up the veggies.. Also use jarred or homemade marinara sauce and you can make this in no time at all..
